headline: Roundtable Calls for Science-Based Regulatory Reforms to Accelerate Safe Adoption of GM and GE Crops in India
fullText:
Ministry of Agriculture &

Roundtable Calls for Science-Based Regulatory Reforms to Accelerate Safe Adoption of GM and GE Crops in India

26 JUL 2026 6:09PM by PIB Delhi

The Trust for Advancement of Agricultural Sciences (TAAS) in collaboration with Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), and the Federation of Seed Industry of India (FSII), organized a high-level Roundtable on "Reforms in Regulations and Approval of Genetically Modified (GM) and Genome-Edited (GE) Crop Plants." The event brought together >80 participants including policymakers, agricultural scientists, regulators, industry leaders, economists, and international experts, to deliberate on modernizing India's agricultural biotechnology regulatory framework.

Dr M.L. Jat, Secretary, DARE and Director General, ICAR, who presided over the event, appreciated the collaborative initiative in bringing together all key stakeholders for a constructive dialogue on an issue of national importance. He reiterated ICAR's steadfast commitment to advancing science-led, evidence-based agricultural innovation and emphasized the need for a balanced regulatory system that facilitates the safe deployment of modern biotechnologies to achieve food and nutritional security, climate resilience, and sustainable agricultural growth. The Roundtable was co-chaired by Dr. R.S. Paroda, Chairman, TAAS, and Dr. M. Ramasami, Founder Chairman, Rasi Seeds (P) Ltd.

India established a comprehensive multi-tiered regulatory framework for transgenic crops under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 and Rules, 1989, today the regulatory ecosystem involves multiple competent authorities, including Institutional Biosafety Committees (IBSCs), the Review Committee on Genetic Manipulation (RCGM) under the Department of Biotechnology (DBT), the Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee (GEAC) under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), ICAR and other concerned ministries and state governments. Nonetheless, rapid advances in genome-editing technologies, including CRISPR-CAS based systems, evolving global regulatory practices and the growing need for climate-resilient and sustainable agriculture necessitate a review and modernization of India’s regulatory framework for GM and GE crops. While India has introduced a differentiated regulatory approach for certain categories of gene-edited products, further reforms are required to improve clarity, harmonization and predictability across the regulatory system. The Roundtable meeting was held to develop a roadmap for efficient approvals of GM/GE crops intended for the national needs, ensuring regulatory efficiency and biosafety standards.

In the inaugural session of the meeting, Dr. Paresh Verma, Director General, FSII, gave the welcome address, while Dr. Bhag Mal, Secretary, TAAS, set the context by underscoring the urgent need to modernize India's regulatory framework in view of climate change, food and nutritional security, sustainable agriculture, and rapid advances in biotechnology. The inaugural session featured keynote lectures by Dr C.D. Mayee, President, South Asia Biotechnology Centre (SABC), on the imperative for regulatory reforms; Dr. Rhodora Romero-Aldemita, Executive Director, ISAAA Inc., spoke on global developments and harmonization of regulatory frameworks; and Mr. Graham Brookes, Agricultural Economist, PG Economics Ltd., UK, presented evidence on the economic benefits of GM and genome-edited crops worldwide.

Two Technical Sessions, moderated by Dr Ashok Singh and Dr Rajvir Rathi, facilitated focused, evidence-based discussions, enabling participants to arrive at a broad consensus on major regulatory reforms needed to make India's biotechnology regulatory system more efficient, transparent, science-based, and globally competitive.

Participants noted that while India has developed robust scientific capabilities and over three decades of experience in biosafety regulation, the regulatory framework must evolve to keep pace with advances in biotechnology, particularly genome editing, while maintaining the highest standards of biosafety and environmental protection. The Roundtable called for a science-based, transparent, efficient, and risk-proportionate regulatory framework with streamlined, time-bound approval processes accessible to both public and private innovators. It also emphasized that timely adoption of safe GM and GE crops is vital for enhancing climate resilience, productivity, nutritional security, farmer incomes, and the global competitiveness of Indian agriculture.

Dr. M. Ramasami stressed that an efficient, transparent, and predictable regulatory system is essential to translate scientific breakthroughs into technologies that benefit farmers, strengthen India's seed sector, and enhance the country's global competitiveness in agricultural innovation.

In his remarks, Dr N.K. Singh emphasized the need for enhanced funding by the Department of Biotechnology (DBT), establishing accredited laboratories, and developing a comprehensive national policy on biotechnology.

In his concluding remarks as Co-Chair, Dr. R.S. Paroda observed that India possesses the scientific expertise and institutional capacity to become a global leader in agricultural biotechnology. He emphasized that the recommendations emerging from the Roundtable should serve as the basis for modernizing India's regulatory framework and creating an enabling policy environment that promotes responsible innovation while safeguarding human health, biodiversity, and the environment. He further stressed the need to review existing multiple guidelines to simplify testing procedures.

The recommendations emerging from the Roundtable will be consolidated into a comprehensive policy document for submission to the concerned Ministries and regulatory authorities to support evidence-based reforms in the regulation and approval of GM and genome-edited crop plants in India.

headline: India’s Partition Was the Greatest Blunder of History; Retrieval of PoJK the Only Pending Issue Between India and Pakistan: Dr. Jitendra Singh
fullText:
Ministry of Science & Technology

India’s Partition Was the Greatest Blunder of History; Retrieval of PoJK the Only Pending Issue Between India and Pakistan: Dr. Jitendra Singh

PM Narendra Modi transformed India’s defence strategy from a reactive approach to a decisive proactive response against external aggression, says Union Minister Jitendra Singh on 27th Kargil Vijay Diwas

Kargil Vijay Diwas is a Reminder of the Nation’s Unwavering Commitment to Safeguard India’s Unity and Sovereignty: Dr. Jitendra Singh

Peace, Development and Strong National Security Have Changed Jammu & Kashmir’s Trajectory, Says Dr. Jitendra Singh

26 JUL 2026 5:27PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology, Earth Sciences and Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh today described India's Partition as "the greatest blunder of history" and said that the retrieval of Pakistan-occupied Jammu & Kashmir (PoJK) remains the only pending issue between India and Pakistan. He said the security landscape of the country has undergone a decisive transformation under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, with India's response to external aggression evolving from a reactive approach to one marked by resolve, preparedness and decisive action.

Dr. Jitendra Singh was addressing the 27th Kargil Vijay Diwas commemoration organised by the Jammu Kashmir Peoples' Forum in collaboration with the POJK Youth Forum, a unit of Mirpur Balidan Bhawan Samity, at the Kashmiri Cultural Centre, New Delhi. Member of Parliament Ms. Bansuri Swaraj attended the programme as the Guest of Honour, while Col. K.K. Sharma (SC, SM & Bar), a Kargil War Veteran, presided over the function. The event was organised under the leadership of Sh. Mahinder Mehta, Convenor of the Jammu Kashmir Peoples' Forum, along with the POJK Youth Forum, to pay homage to the brave soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice during the 1999 Kargil conflict.

Describing Kargil Vijay Diwas as an occasion of remembrance as well as renewed national resolve, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the victory symbolises the indomitable courage of the Indian Armed Forces and the nation's unwavering commitment to safeguard India's unity, sovereignty and territorial integrity. He said the lessons of Kargil remain relevant even today as the challenges confronting the country continue to demand constant vigilance and national unity.

Tracing the historical context of the Kargil conflict, the Minister said the events of 1999 cannot be viewed in isolation but as part of a prolonged sequence of developments beginning with the Partition. Calling Partition "the greatest blunder of history", he said the decision inflicted immense human suffering, displaced millions and laid the foundation for decades of hostility, including the wars of 1947, 1965, 1971 and Kargil, as well as sustained cross-border terrorism and proxy warfare. He also recalled the displacement of Kashmiri Pandits as one of the gravest humanitarian tragedies witnessed in independent India.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said India has fundamentally transformed its national security approach over the last decade. He said the Government adopted a policy of zero tolerance towards terrorism, strengthened border management and replaced a reactive security doctrine with a proactive strategy capable of responding decisively to external aggression. This shift, he said, has significantly enhanced national confidence and strengthened India's ability to safeguard its territorial integrity.

The Minister said peace and development share a mutually reinforcing relationship and pointed to the unprecedented transformation witnessed in Jammu & Kashmir in recent years. He referred to major infrastructure projects, including railway connectivity to the Kashmir Valley, the world's highest railway bridge, new AIIMS institutions, long-pending irrigation projects and accelerated development initiatives that have improved the quality of life and strengthened public confidence. He said sustained peace has enabled rapid development, while development itself has emerged as a powerful force for lasting stability.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the country's growing self-reliance in defence manufacturing has further strengthened national security. He noted that India has substantially expanded indigenous defence production, developed advanced strategic capabilities and emerged as a significant exporter of defence equipment, reflecting the country's technological progress and strategic confidence under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Referring to developments across the Line of Control, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the pace of development in Jammu & Kashmir has become a source of inspiration for people living in Pakistan-occupied Jammu & Kashmir. Recalling the unanimous Parliamentary Resolution of 1994, he said there is no issue between India and Pakistan except the retrieval of Pakistan-occupied Jammu & Kashmir, reaffirming that PoJK is an integral part of India.

Paying glowing tributes to the martyrs of the Kargil War, Dr. Jitendra Singh called upon the younger generation to draw inspiration from their courage, patriotism and selfless sacrifice. He said the spirit of Kargil continues to inspire every Indian to work towards a stronger, secure, self-reliant and developed nation while remaining steadfast in the collective commitment to preserve India's unity, sovereignty and national interests.

headline: As Monsoon Arrives, Rajnandgaon is Ready to #CatchTheRain Through Mission Jal Raksha
fullText:
Ministry of Jal Shakti

As Monsoon Arrives, Rajnandgaon is Ready to #CatchTheRain Through Mission Jal Raksha

Science-driven and community-led initiative demonstrates how rainwater harvesting and groundwater recharge can ensure long-term water security

26 JUL 2026 1:55PM by PIB Delhi

As the nationwide #CatchTheRain campaign gains momentum with the onset of the monsoon, districts across the country are harnessing seasonal rainfall to strengthen water security and promote source sustainability. Among them, Rajnandgaon district in Chhattisgarh has emerged as a frontrunner, demonstrating that preparedness is the foundation of effective water conservation. Through its pioneering Mission Jal Raksha, the district has developed scientific infrastructure, mobilized communities, and implemented innovative groundwater recharge interventions to ensure that every possible raindrop is captured, conserved, and channelled back into the aquifers. Simply put, Rajnandgaon is monsoon-ready—and ready to catch the rain.

Long before the first raindrop touches the ground, Rajnandgaon has prepared its landscape to capture, conserve and recharge every possible drop. Through Mission Jal Raksha, the district has created a scientific and community-driven framework that ensures rainwater is not allowed to flow away as runoff but is channelled back into the earth to replenish precious groundwater reserves.

The initiative combines advanced technologies such as GIS mapping, remote sensing, aquifer mapping, Digital Elevation Models (DEM) and ridge-to-valley planning to identify the most effective locations for groundwater recharge. This scientific approach has been complemented by innovative field interventions, including the conversion of defunct borewells into recharge shafts and the construction of mini percolation tanks integrated with deep injection wells, enabling rainwater to reach deep aquifers even in hard-rock terrain.

What truly distinguishes Mission Jal Raksha is that it has evolved into a people's movement. Farmers, women, youth, Gram Panchayats and local communities have actively embraced water budgeting, awareness campaigns and behavioural change initiatives, making Jan Bhagidari the driving force behind sustainable water management. Crop diversification has further strengthened these efforts, with nearly 70 per cent of summer paddy cultivation shifting to less water-intensive crops, reducing pressure on groundwater while improving agricultural sustainability.

The district's preparedness is reflected in measurable outcomes. More than 60,000 water conservation and recharge structures have been created across 662 villages, over 500 defunct borewells have been converted into recharge shafts, 600+ injection wells integrated with 1,700+ mini percolation tanks have been established, and more than 2,500 water bodies have been geo-tagged. These interventions have generated over 51 lakh person-days of employment and contributed to an average groundwater level rise of approximately 2.04 metres, strengthening irrigation and drinking water security across the district.

As the #CatchTheRain campaign continues to inspire citizens across the country to "Conserve every drop," Rajnandgaon exemplifies how advance planning, scientific interventions and Jan Bhagidari can transform the monsoon into a lasting source of water security. Every recharge structure, every revived borewell and every conserved drop reflects the shared commitment of the community and the district to transforming today's rainfall into tomorrow's groundwater security.

Mission Jal Raksha reinforces that catching the rain is not merely a seasonal activity but a sustained commitment towards source sustainability, climate resilience and a water-secure future.

Rajnandgaon isn't waiting for the rain—it's ready to capture every drop.
